title: Why So Toxic? Measuring and Triggering Toxic Behavior in Open-Domain Chatbots*
measurement_description: The paper measures the tendency of open-domain chatbots to generate toxic responses when prompted with queries on polarizing topics, including religion. Specifically, it evaluated how non-toxic or low-toxicity queries mentioning religious groups (e.g., Jews) or religiously-coded phrases (e.g., 'religion of peace') could trigger highly toxic outputs from the models.
findings: Queries about religious groups (e.g., Jews) or containing religiously-coded phrases (e.g., 'religion of peace'), even when not toxic themselves, were found to be effective triggers for generating highly toxic responses from open-domain chatbots. This highlights a vulnerability where seemingly benign, religion-related inputs can elicit harmful model behavior.
